terms.name: data subject
terms.def: an identified or identifiable natural person whose personal data are processed

terms.name: controller
terms.def: the natural or legal person which determines the purposes and means of the processing

terms.name: personal data
terms.def: any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person

terms.name: erasure
terms.def: destruction of the personal data so that they are no longer available to the controller

terms.name: processing
terms.def: any operation performed on personal data; the Article does not fix its boundaries here

anchor.span: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller the erasure of personal data
anchor.note: the right is stated before the grounds; the grounds are conditions, not a separate position

conditions: where one of the grounds (a)-(f) applies

anchor.span: the controller shall have the obligation to erase personal data
anchor.note: correlative of a1; written as a duty rather than restating the right

conditions: the personal data have been made public
taking account of available technology and the cost of implementation

anchor.span: take reasonable steps, including technical measures, to inform controllers which are processing the personal
anchor.note: the counterparty is a class of controllers, not a named party; the term used is a placeholder for that class

conditions: to the extent that processing is necessary for one of the purposes (a)-(e)

anchor.span: Paragraphs 1 and 2 shall not apply to the extent that processing is necessary
anchor.note: recorded as an atom only so that the carve-out is visible; it defeats a1/a2 and v0.1 has no construct for defeat

escapes.detail: the carve-out cannot be closed: 'processing' is defined in Art. 4 and not in this corpus, and the Article's own five purposes are open-textured; more importantly, v0.1 has no 'defeats' relation, so this atom is recorded as an ordinary position and does not actually defeat a1/a2
